correctness.rationale: Reconstruct inclusion-exclusion interpolation F_v(x)=sum(-1)^j binom(v+j,j) x^underline{j}. Uniform convergence and the telescoping product divided-difference show, on odd x,y, the difference quotient is odd for all even v. The odd-input isometry therefore maps 1+2Z2 bijectively onto 2Z2 and has a unique zero, giving exact valuations. Recurrence modulo 8 proves D_(2t)≡1-vt. Legendre's theorem gives one odd class per even valuation shell and one even class when v=2 mod4, and root neighborhoods bound the density-tail error. The actual embedded CHECK.py passed 176 full finite modulus/parameter checks and 32,752 odd-input fibers. Finite checks are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full Ulas 2023 original paper pp.231–236, especially p.236 Problems 4.1–4.2 and Question 4.3, poses the even-parameter three-square classification, valuation and density questions without their solutions. The new theorem establishes all of these uniformly for even v>=4. O'Desky–Richman arXiv:2012.04615 develops p-adic interpolation for different derangement-type sequences, not the entire even-v generalized derangement three-square spectrum. The known fixed-parameter result at v=2, classical v=0, and published classical dyadic fiber classifications are acknowledged and excluded. Actual semantic queries were run on indexed mathematical findings and bibliographic literature, but unindexed implicit stronger results remain a specific residual risk.
residual_risks: The publicly indexed contemporary classical-derangement source trees were inaccessible for complete full-text inspection; no whole-document NOT_COVERING assertion is made.
A yet-unindexed paper or an implicit specialization of a broad generalized-derangement framework may overlap; no assertion of exhaustive global priority is made.
The unique root has an algorithmic 2-adic description rather than a closed elementary formula.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the natural open even-parameter generalized-derangement three-squares questions recorded in Ulas (2023), by giving a complete computable exception classification, exact valuation isometry and exact two-phase density for every even v>=4. The first new case v=4 has density 1/24 and v=6 has density 1/6. The result is not a textbook local congruence or isolated finite computation, and known v=0 and v=2 cases are excluded.
